artboards.title: The door — describe it, and choose Build or Spawn
Goal — what it read back, and the one thing it will not assume
Build — the primary state. Four settled, one proposed
Choose — an alternative previewed, and what it drags with it
Parameters — the one value the engine could not settle
Collection — 1→1, N→N, N→1, and never N copies of a node
Spawn — the same engine, and honest about who chose what
When it does not work — pending, refusal, stale, failed, no model
Hard content — fifteen steps, a long id, five ports
Narrower, and still — three widths and every movement off
Done — the artifact, and who settled what

annotations.text:
THE LIVING PIPELINE — ten boards, one fixture, one session.

A researcher says what they have and what they want; the RESOLVER builds the pipeline and the conversation hands it over one decision at a time. The model never authors the graph, the YAML or a coordinate — it produces a typed Goal, or picks from candidates the server supplied.

Every count, name, tier and author on all ten boards comes from one dict, `S` in build_living.py. Observatory palette lifted by value from frontend/src/tokens.css — tokens.css is UNCHANGED by this design and no hue is added.

Plan: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-07-the-living-pipeline.md, Task 1.

THE ONE IDEA: THERE IS NO INSPECTOR.

The conversation IS the inspector, because every object on the canvas was put there by a decision that is already in the transcript. Select a node and the log scrolls to the decision that created it; select a card and the object highlights.

That is what dissolves the tab strip. The old builder stacked four bands of chrome above the first sentence anybody wanted to read — a panel header, Builder's three tabs, Rail's own three, and the gate panel. The living builder has ONE strip and no tabs anywhere beneath it, because the rail has nothing to switch between.

WHAT THIS REOPENS FROM THE 2026-08-29 CANVAS — one thing, named.

`impl-settled` says: NO PROMPT BOX ON THE POPULATED PAGE. Creation is monthly; checking a run is daily. The prompt lives in the empty state and the command palette. Never as a banner.

THAT RULE STANDS AND THIS IS NOT AN EXCEPTION TO IT. What it forbids is a CREATION affordance on a page about something else. The rail here is not a prompt box: it is the provenance record of this pipeline, made navigable, and it is the only place a tier-4 question can be asked. It appears on an AUTHORING session and nowhere else — /build?draft=<id> on an old manual draft opens the canvas without it.

Two rules from that note are load-bearing here and are NOT reopened:
· the left steps list stays deleted. Two columns, never three — and the transcript must not become a steps list wearing a different border, which is why an accepted decision collapses to one line and history sits above the fold.
· settings live in the card on the node. The conversation ASKS a question; it never LISTS values. Asking and listing are different, and two lists of one thing is what was removed.

THE TRANSCRIPT IS A RULED LOG, NOT A CHAT.

Bubbles were the shipped artboard's form — build_boards.py::RAIL_ASSISTANT, a right-aligned #122029 bubble — and they are wrong here for a reason that is not taste: a chat log has nowhere to put WHO DECIDED THIS. A hairline with a tick per turn does.

An accepted decision COLLAPSES to one line carrying its name, its step, and who settled it. LivingDense is the proof: eleven decisions in the space two expanded cards would take, with a scannable settled / model chose / you chose column. Expanded, that is fifteen tall cards nobody scrolls through.

THE LOG SCROLLS TO THE PENDING BLOCK. History sits above the fold. That rule was found by rendering, not by reading — four boards drew full history AND a tall block, which is a state the product never shows.

ONE SLOT, ONE BOX — and hover is never the only route.

The first LivingChoose drew HISAT2 as a SECOND node below STAR with a connector between them, and it read as a pipeline that had gained a module rather than one whose aligner was being swapped. `n-bswap` on the 2026-08-29 canvas had already settled this — TRIMGALORE struck through, HISAT2 IN PLACE — and departing from it was the mistake.

The canvas shows what the graph WOULD BECOME, not a comparison widget. Comparing is the rail's job and it already has the candidate list. So: one box in the slot, the tool leaving named in its footer, and the ribbon drawn straight THROUGH the step being removed — the picture of the reads reaching the aligner directly. Nothing on the canvas moves.

`impl-walkbugs` records a palette unreachable by keyboard, and an option list whose preview fires only on hover repeats that exactly. So the FOCUSED option carries the same ring and throws the same substitution as the hovered one. The recommended option is marked IN WORDS, never by colour alone.

COLLECTION IS DRAWN ON THE WIRE — LivingCollect.

§1.7: one logical channel, never N nodes and never N wires. Today a per-sample channel and a run-scoped one are the same single stroke, so the canvas cannot say the one thing a researcher most needs to know about their own data.

  1 → 1   one stroke
  N → N   a three-strand ribbon, 12px band
  N → 1   the ribbon CONVERGES into one stroke at a wide port

The convergence is the picture of .collect(). Three strands whether N is 12 or 12,000 — the COUNT is on the source node, never on the wire, and `×12 samples` is drawn only where measurement.n_samples supplies it. Otherwise `×N items` and nothing more. No filename or sample id ever reaches Mendel to decorate a canvas (invariant 15).

AUTHOR IS DRAWN AS STROKE. TIER IS DRAWN AS COLOUR.

`impl-inv` fixes colour to the tier ladder — settled spends none, measured is amber, open is red. So author cannot have a hue without destroying what colour already says. Plan 3B settled the other axis: certainty is drawn as STROKE. This is that, applied to the node's left bar.

  solid          the resolver settled it — the common case, and it says nothing
  dashed         a model chose it — the one that must be visible
  solid + notch  a person chose it — a benchmark mark at the bar's midpoint

The same three marks are the transcript's ticks, so the rail and the canvas are one language read in two directions. An amber dashed bar composes correctly: measured, chosen by a model.

SEE LivingSpawn. The MODEL text tag was removed from that node during this pass — the bar IS the statement, and saying it twice weakens the encoding the board exists to prove.

BEYOND ABOUT SIX STEPS YOU PAN — LivingDense, and it took three tries.

First version wrapped a fifteen-step chain onto three rows to make it fit, which put a wire running RIGHT TO LEFT on a canvas whose first law is left-to-right. `dag-core` does layered layout and never produces one. Second version shrank it to fit and every label went with it.

The honest answer is the third: four columns at 1:1, the minimap saying where you are, and the transcript carrying all fifteen. THAT IS THE FINDING — beyond about six steps the canvas is where you look at ONE PART of a pipeline and the conversation is where you read the whole of it. It is also the strongest argument for the collapsed log.

None of the three is distinguishable in the HTML.

SIX DOMAIN EVENTS, FIVE EXISTING MOVEMENTS, NO NEW CURVE — LivingQuiet.

  proposal_shown       settle 200ms   the card, and the ghost on the canvas
  proposal_accepted    settle 200ms   the node at its blueprint position
  edge_committed       grow-x 520ms   first paint only, keyed on the edge's identity
  parameter_committed  settle 200ms   the value row, and its line in the artifact
  proposal_rejected    —              the ghost is removed. Nothing moves to say so
  validation_changed   —              the status line changes. Numbers never tween

A ghost is STATIC. `dash` — marching ants — is the RUNNING movement and borrowing it here would spend the page's one claim that something is happening right now.

NOTHING HERE IS ONLY AN ANIMATION. A proposal arriving is a dashed node and a card; accepted, a solid node and a collapsed row. Both are states and both are true in a screenshot. Reduced motion drops the fade and keeps the edge.

1180 AND 1000, AND THE SECOND ONE IS A THIRD BREAKPOINT.

`rs-page-1` puts them at 1180 and 760 and says not to add one without content that needs it. This has some: a proposal card carries two actions side by side and the canvas beside it carries a 172px column, and under about 1000px those cannot both exist. At 1180 they still can, so the rail narrows to 360 there and stacks lower down.

THE CONVERSATION GOES ON TOP when it stacks — it is where the next thing to do lives. Stacking canvas-first puts an empty graph above the only actionable thing on the page. `order`, not DOM order: the canvas stays first for a screen reader.

A RAIL STACKS, IT DOES NOT OVERLAY. An overlay drawer hides the graph the conversation is talking about.

The breakpoints are IN the artboards' shared head, so `_prev.py --width 900` renders the stacked layout rather than a squeezed 1400. A board that cannot be rendered narrow cannot be checked narrow.

THE ARTIFACT NEEDS NO NEW SURFACE — LivingDone.

`impl-settled`: the second view of the canvas is the ARTIFACT (pipeline.yml), not a list. So the living pipeline's YAML preview is the toggle that already exists, and what is new is only that it GREW while you answered — the lines your last answer wrote carry a left rule and a tint, then settle to ordinary artifact text.

The server serialises it. `pipeline_file.dump` is the only canonical writer and the browser diffs successive text for PRESENTATION only. Preview is not Keep: it sets no `kept` flag, writes no file, stages no modules and makes no gate available.

A MODEL — NOTHING is the line this board exists for. On a pipeline where no tier-4 choice needed one, the completion block says so in the same table that credits the engine and the person. Provenance is per decision, and a summary that could only ever say `AI-assisted` is not one.

Browsing is NOT redrawn: BuilderBrowse.dc.html and BuilderPort.dc.html are established artboards for the same overlays, reached the same way, and redrawing them would create a second specification for one screen.

WHAT IS MVP HERE, AND WHAT IS DEFERRED.

MVP: one primary left-to-right chain, one pending mutation proposal at a time, the three collection shapes, Build and Spawn over one proposal engine, the values card, the Artifact toggle, Run through the existing sheet.

DEFERRED AND NOT DRAWN: branch creation, branch labels, conditionals, loops, rejoining. An auxiliary branch that the resolver's own blueprint contains is LAID OUT and drawn with neutral wires — LivingDense has five — but there is no control for authoring one. General branch authoring is a later design problem and drawing a control for it here would make it look decided.

ALSO NOT DRAWN: token streaming, collaborative cursors, a phone. These are desk screens; the rules degrade to a tablet and stop there, deliberately.

AN INPUT IS DRAWN WHERE IT ENTERS — not in a left-hand gutter.

The first version pinned every source beside the entry channels, so `genome.index.star` sat at the far left with a wire dragged across the whole graph. That says two false things: that the index is something you have at the START of the analysis, and that it is an entry channel like the reads.

It is neither. It enters AT the aligner. `dag-core` does layered layout, so a source whose only consumer is at layer 2 belongs at layer 1 — beside the steps it is contemporary with, with a short wire into the port that needs it.

This generalises: an input can arrive at ANY point in the chain. A GTF that only featureCounts reads, a blacklist BED, a panel manifest — each is drawn in the layer before its consumer, and a step gaining a bound input gains a source node THERE rather than at the front. LivingParam shows the other half: an input nothing has bound yet has no source node at all, only a finding.

Operator, 2026-09-07.
